verdict.line: You lose lane if you trade into his Q-stack-into-pull chained with his W (Path Maker) stun, or get caught by his R (All Out) near a wall; you win by poking at 625 range with Q (Parrrley), stacking Grog-Soaked Blade poison, and outscaling him once Essence Reaver and Lord Dominik's Regards come online.

brief.thesis: K'Sante's lane threat is built entirely around a CC chain: Q (Ntofo Strikes) grants a stack on hit, and at 2 stacks it fires a shockwave that pulls you in, which he can follow with W (Path Maker)'s charge-up stun dash to land a full engage. That's why the measured data calls this an even lane (51.5% Gangplank win rate over 237 games) but gives K'Sante the solo-kill edge — he wins the all-in, not the poke war. Gangplank has no proactive counter to the pull, only W (Remove Scurvy) to cleanse the stun afterward on an 18-22s cooldown, so the matchup is decided by whether you respect his 450-range engage tools or walk into them.

theirWindow.what: At 2 stacks his Q (Ntofo Strikes) fires a shockwave that pulls you in, and if his W (Path Maker) is also up he can chain straight into the stun dash. Walk out of his 450-range Q before the second stack lands, or hold W (Remove Scurvy) to cleanse the stun if you get caught.

yourWindow.what: Without the stun dash he has no way to lock you down after a pull, so step up and poke with Q (Parrrley) and let Grog-Soaked Blade poison tick while he's forced to either eat autos or disengage.

start.why: The most-picked start into K'Sante (72.4% pick, 50.7% WR over 205 games) — the extra AD and sustain let you trade autos into his short 3.5s Q (Ntofo Strikes) without losing the poke war on lane sustain.

boots.why: Picked 32.9% of the time at a 54.1% win rate — flat physical damage reduction blunts his autos and Q (Ntofo Strikes) chip damage, which is how he wins the lane if you let him stack Q freely.

core.why: Gives you the mana sustain to spam Q (Parrrley) on its 5s cooldown all lane plus crit/AD scaling, so you can keep poking from 625 range instead of running dry and being forced into his 450-range engage tools.

The highest-performing version of this build path (73.1% WR over 26 games) — lethality and the execute threshold let you finish him through his tanky stat line once Parrrley and your poison have chipped him down.
Armor penetration scales against K'Sante's naturally tanky build, cutting through the resistances that otherwise make your autos and Parrrley fall off in extended fights.

situational.when: you're ahead and snowballing and want to convert crit chance into pure damage instead of more penetration
he's landing his R (All Out) engage on you consistently and you need lifesteal to survive the follow-up
he's leaning on E (Footwork)'s shield to tank your poke through the laning phase
you'd rather have lifesteal sustain than armor and he isn't out-trading you with autos

runes.keystoneWhy: Deathfire Touch's burn stacks every time you land an ability, so each Parrrley poke adds a DOT on top of your passive Grog-Soaked Blade poison — you win extended trades through sustained magic damage instead of needing to stand in his Q/W range to out-auto him.

summoners.why: Flash+Teleport posts a 62.3% win rate (21.5% pick) in this matchup, well above Flash+Ignite's 50% despite Ignite being more popular (77.5% pick) — since the lane is defensive-shaped with K'Sante holding the solo-kill edge, Teleport lets you skip forcing early kills, reset freely for Doran's items, and still arrive for sieges once Essence Reaver and The Collector come online.

playing.title: Poke outside his engage range
playing.detail: Q (Parrrley) reaches 625, while his Q (Ntofo Strikes) only hits 450 — land poke and poison stacks from max range instead of trading autos where he can start stacking Ntofo Strikes.

playing.title: Count his Ntofo Strikes stacks
playing.detail: Every Q hit grants a stack, and at 2 stacks he fires a shockwave that pulls you in; disengage once he's sitting on 1 stack instead of letting the second one land for free.

playing.title: Hold W for his stun, not poke
playing.detail: Remove Scurvy clears CC and heals but sits on an 18-22s cooldown depending on rank — save it for his W (Path Maker) stun dash rather than burning it on chip damage.

playing.title: Never fight near a wall
playing.detail: His R (All Out) knocks you back through any wall in its path before he dashes after you empowered, so a trade that's fine in open lane can turn lethal next to terrain.

playing.title: Use R off-lane to deny resets
playing.detail: Cannon Barrage has no cast-range limit and slows while dealing damage over time anywhere on the map — zone his jungler's ganks or chip his health during recalls instead of hoarding it only for lane kills.

playing.title: Build through his armor
playing.detail: Lord Dominik's Regards and The Collector cut through the resistances he stacks as a tank, which is exactly where plain AD items would fall off against him.

playing.title: Scale, don't force all-ins
playing.detail: The measured data gives K'Sante the solo-kill edge in this matchup, so play for farm, poke damage, and your Essence Reaver core rather than trying to win the all-in he's built for.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, boots, rune pages, and summoner spell win rates above are pulled directly from measured Gangplank vs K'Sante top lane games on the current patch; the CC-chain tell, trade spacing, and itemization reasoning are this coach's own read on why those numbers look the way they do.
